title: Revenue Share per Category Using Window SUM
description: For each individual sale, compute its **percentage contribution to the total revenue of its own category**. Show product name, category, sale amount, and category_share_pct rounded to 2 decimal places.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE sales (sale_id INT, product_name VARCHAR(100), category VARCHAR(50), amount DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO sales VALUES (1,'Laptop','Electronics',1200.00),(2,'Phone','Electronics',800.00),(3,'Tablet','Electronics',400.00),(4,'Headphones','Electronics',200.00),(5,'Shirt','Clothing',50.00),(6,'Pants','Clothing',80.00),(7,'Jacket','Clothing',150.00),(8,'Hammer','Hardware',30.00),(9,'Drill','Hardware',120.00),(10,'Wrench','Hardware',25.00);
solution_sql: SELECT product_name, category, amount, ROUND(amount * 100.0 / SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY category), 2) AS category_share_pct FROM sales ORDER BY category, amount DESC

test_cases.description: 10 sales each showing its % of category total. Electronics total=2600, Clothing=280, Hardware=175.

hints: SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY category) returns the category total on every row in that category — without grouping or reducing the row count.
Divide each row's amount by the partition sum and multiply by 100 to compute the percentage share.
explanation: SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY category) computes the total sales per category and stamps it on every row — the result set remains 10 rows. Dividing individual amount by this total gives the proportion. Electronics: Laptop=1200/2600=46.15%, Phone=800/2600=30.77%, Tablet=15.38%, Headphones=7.69%. The window function avoids a self-join and is much more efficient.
